5.0.0.en: Hiram: he is also called Huram in (2 Chr 2:3). Tyre: a great commercial city in Phoenicia, that is, Lebanon, lying on the coast of the Mediterranean Sea.

5.0.1.en: Hiram king of Tyre was a lover of David. So when he learned of his death, he sent senior men of state to console Solomon and congratulate him on assuming the throne in succession to his father, and to confirm the covenants of love and peace between the two of them and between their two peoples.

5.1.0.en: Put them under the soles of his feet: made them subject to him.

5.1.1.en: Solomon answered Hiram with a message in which he explained to him his father David's desire to build a house for the Lord, but his being occupied with many wars with the surrounding countries kept him from fulfilling his desire.

5.1.2.en: Here Solomon made the Gentiles, that is, Hiram, partners in the building of the house of God. He is a type of Christ, who made the Gentiles partners with the Jews in the temple of His body when He died for all, and gives all His true Body and Blood.

5.1.3.en: Solomon here is a type of Christ in the establishment of peace in his days, as Christ bound Satan after His victory over him by the Cross and gave peace to those who believe in Him.

5.2.0.en: Behold, I purpose to build an house: I have intended to build a house.

5.2.1.en: Solomon showed Hiram the stability and peace which his kingdom enjoyed, for there were no enemies or evildoers to harm the kingdom, which allowed him to decide to build a house for the Lord as God had charged David his father (2 Sam 7:12).

5.3.0.en: Cedar from Lebanon: huge, tall, evergreen trees that live long, and their wood is bitter, that is, not subject to decay, so they are suitable for building great buildings and can be painted.

5.3.1.en: The Sidonians: the inhabitants of Sidon, which lies north of Tyre and belongs to its king.

5.3.2.en: Solomon asked the king of Tyre to commission his men living in Sidon, which was under him, to cut cedar trees from Lebanon, and Solomon would send his men to work with the men of the king of Tyre, and he would pay the wages of the Sidonians as the king of Tyre determined, because the children of Israel were not skilled at cutting trees like the people of the city of Sidon. This shows Solomon's wisdom in making use of the talents of others in cooperating with him and his honesty in not exploiting them, but paying their wages as their king Hiram saw fit, that is, full wages. Solomon's importing of timber from Hiram and giving in return supplies such as wheat, barley, wine, and oil (2 Chr 2:10) was the economic exchange that resulted from the friendship between Tyre and the children of Israel and strengthened the bond between them.

5.3.3.en: How beautiful is cooperation! It lets you benefit from the experience of those around you and achieve greater success, but it needs humility, as Solomon, the owner of a great kingdom, humbled himself in his words to the king of Tyre. By humility you win those around you and achieve for yourself and for others what they desire.

5.4.0.en: Hiram welcomed taking part in the work with the son of his friend David, and saw that he was a good and wise son and a gift from God to the people of Israel. It was the custom of the pagans to believe that every country has its gods and that it is proper for each country to respect the god of the other, so he said "Blessed be the Lord," not because he believed in Him but out of mere respect.

5.5.0.en: Fir: a large tree found in Syria and Palestine, whose wood is used for building ships and building houses along with cedar wood.

5.5.1.en: Hiram responded to Solomon and agreed to supply him with all he wanted of cedar and fir timber. It is understood from this that Solomon asked for kinds of timber, not only cedar wood, but as the Book of Chronicles mentions, he asked for fir and algum wood (2 Chr 2:8).

5.6.1.en: Hiram added that he would order his men to cut the timber from the trees, gather it in bundles, throw them on the waters of the sea, and drive them floating on the surface of the waters, to deliver them to Solomon's men at the place Solomon would appoint, and from this place Solomon and his men could carry this timber overland to wherever he wanted. In return for the price of the timber Hiram sent him, Solomon sent Hiram the food supplies for his palace.

5.7.0.en: Measure (cor): a measure for liquids and grain whose volume is approximately 229 liters.

5.7.2.en: Pure oil: it is the purest of oils because there are no impurities in it, since the oil is extracted by beating the fruit and not by pressing it.

5.7.3.en: Hiram carried out the agreement between him and Solomon, so Solomon obtained all his needs of cedar and fir timber from the king of Tyre, and in return supplied him with the food supplies he asked for, giving him each year, throughout the period of preparing the timber, twenty thousand measures of wheat and twenty measures of oil. This, of course, is apart from the wages of the workers belonging to Hiram, which are mentioned in (2 Chr 2:10), where we find a larger quantity of oil that Solomon provided.

5.7.4.en: We see by this that Solomon feeds his people the Jews working with him, and likewise the Gentiles belonging to the king of Tyre, with wheat, wine, and oil (2 Chr 2:10). In this he is a type of Christ, who feeds those who believe in Him, whether of Jewish or Gentile origin, with His Body and Blood taken from wheat and wine, and gives them His Holy Spirit, who is symbolized by the oil.

5.8.0.en: The Lord gave Solomon wisdom to maintain his friendship with Hiram, and both succeeded in keeping up relations of mutual affection, and they put that into a covenant that both of them made. The friendship between the two peoples continued until the reign of King Ahab, who married Jezebel the daughter of the king of Sidon (ch. 16:31). So we see that friendship with the surrounding peoples is beneficial, but care must be taken against an increase of closeness that leads the people of God to take on the customs of other peoples and worship their gods, as happened in the days of Ahab.

5.8.1.en: It is very useful to take care to make peace with those around you, for this lets you be occupied with your spiritual worship and your service, in addition to cooperating with them, so that love is established between you and them and you win everyone to God by your love and your working for their comfort.

5.9.0.en: The levy: the workers conscripted for work.

5.9.1.en: Adoniram: see the commentary on (ch. 4:6). Solomon put 30 thousand Israelites to work, sending them in rotation, 10 thousand at a time in a group that stayed to work for a month in Lebanon and returned, so that the men stayed in their houses with their families for two months until the time of the next turn came. This was Solomon's care not to burden the workers, and for the unity and well-being of the family, so that the worker's family would not feel deprived of him. He chose for the children of Israel the cutting of timber, while the non-Jews worked in cutting stones (v. 25); that is, he chose the easier work for his own people out of concern for them. Forced labor meant that a man worked in return for his food and necessary needs, and forced labor was known in great countries for the completion of huge projects, as in Egypt for the building of the pyramids. The treatment of those conscripted was good, especially of the children of Israel, for they were not considered slaves but as hired workers, and they gave a tax to the state for the completion of its great projects, which was part of their wages, because those who conscripted them were the men of war, the princes, and Solomon's assistants, as will come in (ch. 9:22). As for the other group that was conscripted, other than the children of Israel, they were the surrounding peoples subject to Solomon, and their forced labor was considered as tribute that they paid to the Jewish kingdom.

5.9.2.en: The number of workers was thirty thousand out of the total men of the children of Israel, whose number exceeded one million four hundred thousand, that is, a proportion of about 1 to 50. Of the thirty thousand, each ten thousand worked for a month and rested two months in his house to do his own work, such as farming; then the second group went for a month, then the third, and after that the turn of work returned to the first group, which had rested two months. The conscription was limited to the Jews for work outside the Jewish kingdom, that is, with King Hiram, because they would certainly return to their families and lands, while the conscription of the Gentiles was inside the Jewish kingdom, so that they would not flee if he sent them outside the land of Judea to Hiram.

5.9.3.en: Solomon appointed Adoniram as the one responsible for supervising the employment of the labor force, as was also mentioned before in (ch. 4:6). He had also held this post in the days of David, and because of his competence he continued in his work in the days of Solomon, and after that in the days of his son Rehoboam. But because forced labor is an undesirable thing, when Rehoboam sent him to quell a rebellion, they killed him.

5.10.0.en: Solomon set the number of burden-bearers in the transport of stones at seventy thousand and of those hewing stones at eighty thousand, all of them prisoners of war from the other nations, as will come in (ch. 9:20), (2 Chr 8:7-9). These did not have a system of rotation for rest as the Israelite workers did, because they were slaves.

5.11.0.en: The numbers mentioned in the previous verse are the numbers of the workers who carried burdens and cut stones. But the work needed other labor to supervise the execution, organize the work, distribute the workers, monitor performance, and control the movements of the labor force, and the number of these was 3300 overseers.

5.12.0.en: King Solomon commanded that the workers select the stones of large size and high quality from the mountains near Jerusalem, such as Mount Moriah, and prepare them to be squared and smooth, so that they would be suitable for building the house of the Lord.

5.13.0.en: The Giblites: the inhabitants of the city of Gebal, which lies on the Mediterranean Sea about 32 km north of Beirut.

5.13.1.en: Solomon's builders hewed the stones in cooperation with the builders of King Hiram, and the inhabitants of the coastal city of Gebal also took part with them, who had experience in building work in general and in shipbuilding in particular, and the builders also prepared the timber needed for the building.

5.13.2.en: Solomon provided the best materials for building the Temple and the best specialized workers. May we, in our worship of God, offer our best times, and in our giving offer the best we have to God, who gives us all good things, as a simple expression of our love and thanks to Him.

5.13.3.en: The building of the Temple. Note: see the drawings and pictures at the end of the book.

5.13.4.en: Solomon built the house of the Lord and called it the Temple, and that was on Mount Moriah (2 Chr 3:1), which lies in the eastern part of the city of Jerusalem, and in the same place Abraham took Isaac to offer him as a sacrifice to God (Gen 22:2). On Mount Moriah also was the threshingfloor of Araunah the Jebusite, where the angel stood to stop the spread of the plague in the days of David (2 Sam 24:15, 16). Solomon's Temple was built around the year 1000 BC and lasted until the year 586 BC, when the Babylonians destroyed it, and it was rebuilt after the return from the captivity at the beginning of the reign of the kingdom of the Medes and Persians by Zerubbabel in the year 536 BC; then the Greeks destroyed it and the Maccabees renewed it in the year 167 BC; then it was renewed again by Herod the Great in the year 20 BC and lasted until the year 70 AD, when Titus the Roman commander destroyed it, and it was not built afterward and will not be built, as Christ foretold when He said, "Behold, your house is left unto you desolate" (Mt 23:38).

6.0.s.en: (1) The dimensions of the Temple, its stories, and its chambers

6.0.0.en: The month Zif: after the captivity its name became the month "Iyyar," which corresponds to part of the month of April and another part of the month of May. It is the second month of the religious year of the Jews, that is, the eighth month of the civil year.

6.0.1.en: The house: that is, the whole house of the Lord, and sometimes what is meant by it is the Holy Place, that is, the place that only the priests enter, which is in front of the Holy of Holies, in which the ark of the covenant is.

6.0.2.en: The writer of the book teaches us that the four hundred and eightieth year after the departure of the children of Israel from Egypt in the days of Moses corresponds to the fourth year of Solomon's reign. Solomon spent three years completing the gathering of building materials for the Temple, in addition to what he received of materials his father David had prepared, and he also took care in these three years to gather the workers who would build the Temple and to organize them. The four hundred and eighty years include forty years in the wilderness of Sinai in the days of Moses, then the entry of the children of Israel into the land of Canaan and their possession of it in the days of Joshua, then the age of the judges, and after it the age of the kingdom, that is, the kingdom of Saul and then David. The fourth year of Solomon's reign corresponds to about the year 1011 BC.

6.0.3.en: The building of the house began in the second month of the religious year of the Jews, and it was called the house of the Lord because it was set apart for the worship of the Lord, and He is the One who chose it and set its design.

6.0.4.en: It is noticed that the tabernacle of meeting is a type of the body of Christ on earth, that is, His body that would be changed, while Solomon's Temple is a type of the luminous body of Christ that remains forever. The tabernacle of meeting is a type of the Church on earth, because its ground is earthen, while Solomon's Temple is a type of the Church in heaven, because its floor is covered with gold, which is a symbol of heavenly things.

6.1.0.en: The cubit: a unit for measuring lengths, equal to about 50 cm.

6.1.1.en: The house: what is meant by it is the whole Temple, that is, the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies.

6.1.2.en: Its height: that is, its elevation.

6.1.3.en: The dimensions of the Temple were double the dimensions of the tabernacle of meeting, and they were as follows:

6.1.4.en: Length 60 cubits, that is, about 30 meters; width 20 cubits, that is, about 10 meters; height 30 cubits, that is, about 15 meters. It is noticed that these measurements are the clear interior ones, without counting the thickness of the walls. These measurements and the details of the building of the Temple were made known by God to David, who made them known to his son Solomon (1 Chr 28:12). Even so, the dimensions of the Temple are small, because those who enter it are only the priests and high priests, while the outer court is wide, since the people enter it. As for the great height of the Temple, it was the usual thing at that time, since some temples of idols rose higher than this, such as the temple of Artemis at Ephesus.

6.2.0.en: The porch: an entrance, or a roofed hall whose roof rests on columns.

6.2.1.en: The temple of the house: what is meant by it here is the Holy Place, which the priests enter, but sometimes what is meant is the whole house of the Lord. The word "temple" (haykal) is a Sumerian word meaning the great house, and the Sumerians are the ancient inhabitants of the land between the two rivers, that is, present-day Iraq.

6.2.2.en: There was a roofed hall with columns in front of the Temple, ten meters long and five meters wide. The Second Book of Chronicles adds that its height reached sixty meters (2 Chr 3:4). Solomon took care to make this porch tower to a great height, so that the appearance of the house would be very grand among all the buildings. The pagan peoples took care to build lofty temples for their gods, such as the Egyptians in their building of the temple of Karnak.

6.2.3.en: It is noticed that the entrance of the Temple, like the entrance of the tabernacle of meeting, was from the east, while the Holy of Holies, where the ark of the covenant of God was, was in the west; God intended this so that they would not be like the sun-worshipers. In the New Testament, the sanctuary of the Church is in the east, for the following reasons:

6.2.4.en: 1- Because Paradise was in the east.

6.2.5.en: 2- The star appeared to the magi in the east.

6.2.6.en: 3- Christ was born in the land of Judea, that is, in the east.

6.2.7.en: 4- Christ is the Sun of Righteousness, that is, the One who comes from the east.

6.2.8.en: 5- Christ will appear at His Second Coming from the east, as He says that the lightning comes out of the east and shines even unto the west, so shall also the coming of Christ be.

6.2.9.en: That is, what is meant in the Church is to look toward Christ, who appeared in the east and will come at His Second Coming from the east.

6.3.0.en: Windows: openings high in the north and south walls near the roof.

6.3.1.en: Broad: its roof is the thickness of the walls.

6.3.2.en: Narrow lights: over the windows were crossed wooden bars or bars of bronze, or of any metal, to prevent birds from entering.

6.3.3.en: Solomon made small windows in the walls of the house, that is, the Holy Place, and covered them with wooden or metal lattices to let air in or smoke out and at the same time to keep birds from entering.

6.4.1.en: The oracle: the Holy of Holies.

6.4.2.en: Round about: that is, on the north, west, and south sides.

6.4.3.en: He built along the sides of the walls of the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies chambers surrounding them, in three stories one above the other, and each story, that is, floor, contained several rooms. These rooms were on the sides of the Temple, that is, the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies, on the north and south sides and also behind the oracle; that is, the rooms were around the Temple on three sides, and the remaining east side was the door, on which there were of course no rooms. These rooms were used for the needs of the Temple, as vessels, offerings, incense, tithes, and heave offerings were put in them, and they were for the priests' lodging and their meetings with the Levites and the scribes (Jer 36:10, 20). It is noticed that no one lived in the tabernacle of meeting or beside it, so that God might show His greatness and awe, so that everyone feared Him and no one could easily approach Him. But in Solomon's Temple God permitted the priests to dwell in His house, as a preparation for the Church of the New Testament, in which all the people are permitted to enter to receive His Body and Blood and be united with Him.

6.5.0.en: Narrowed rests: plural of a rest, which is an angle or projection in the outer wall of the rooms, since the wall decreases in thickness at the end of the story, leaving a space on which the ends of the timbers can be placed; that is, the wall is thick at the first story, decreases in thickness at the middle story, and again at the upper story.

6.5.1.en: Beams: wooden columns, that is, rafters, laid close together to form the ceiling of the room, or the floor of the room above it.

6.5.2.en: When the walls of the Temple were built, the wall was built thick at the bottom, and at a height of five cubits, that is, at the story following it, he made the thickness of the wall decrease by half a cubit, then after another five cubits of height he made the wall of the Temple decrease by half a cubit up to the roof of the Temple. The same measurements were followed exactly in the opposite wall, that is, the outer wall of the rooms.

6.5.3.en: When building the rooms, Solomon did not want to dig into the walls of the Temple to set the boards forming the roof of the rooms, or the floor of the rooms above them, so as not to weaken the walls of the Temple.

6.5.4.en: So he built the wall of the Temple, which is the inner wall of the rooms, and likewise the outer wall, thick at the bottom, and at a height of five cubits, that is, at the middle story, the thickness of each of the two walls decreases by half a cubit, and thus a space, that is, a projection, is formed in each of the two walls on which the wooden boards are placed, and this is repeated after another five cubits, that is, at the upper story.

6.5.5.en: By this the width of the lower rooms is five cubits, then in the middle story it increases to become six cubits, and in the upper it increases to become seven cubits. So the higher we go, the more the area of the room increases.

6.6.0.en: Hammer: an iron tool for breaking and hewing stones (a pick). Axe: a hatchet.

6.6.1.en: The house was built with whole stones which the workers quarried and hewed in their quarries, that is, in the places from which they were cut, before being brought to the site of the Temple, so that no sound of any iron tool for hewing and dressing the stones was heard in the Temple while it was being built. This means that the work was done in the house of the Lord quietly. That was in fulfillment of God's commandment not to use iron tools in building His altar or His Temple, so that they would not resemble the temples of idols in which these tools are used to make statues (Ex 20:25). The stones are a type of the believers built up as living stones in the body of Christ, that is, the Church, and the hewing of the stones is a type of the sufferings that the believers endure on earth, while in the Temple, which is a type of heaven, there is no hewing in it, that is, no sufferings in it.

6.7.1.en: The means of going up to the middle story and then the upper was through an entrance in the middle room, that is, the one in the middle of the rooms on the right side of the house, the south side, so that the entrance is on your right if you are looking to the east. From this entrance we find a spiral stone stair going up to the middle story, and from it to the upper story.

6.8.0.en: After Solomon finished building the house, he covered its roof with beams and boards of cedar wood.

6.9.2.en: Solomon built the chambers with a height of five cubits, that is, 2.5 meters for each story, so that the height of the three stories is 15 cubits, apart from the thickness of the roofs and floors.

6.9.3.en: The fastening of the chambers to the house with cedar beams, as we explained in (v. 6), was by setting the beams on the rests, that is, the angles or projections formed as a result of the decrease in the thickness of the walls, so that they rested on them and were strong without the need for any digging in the wall of the house.

6.9.4.en: The firmness of the chambers and their attachment to the Temple is a type of the servants who are steadfast in the Church and help in gathering souls to cleave to God. So take care to be steadfast in the Church through the Holy Sacraments and the means of grace, so that you can help others to be bound to the Church and enjoy God's care.

6.10.s.en: (2) The word of the Lord to Solomon at the time of building the Temple

6.10.0.en: During the building of the house, while Solomon was devoting all his energies and the energies of the kingdom to building the Temple of the Lord, the Lord spoke to him, either in a vision, or through Nathan the prophet, or one of the prophets, for the following reasons:

6.10.1.en: 1- To encourage him, because the work was huge, so that he would feel that God was with him, helping him and completing everything for him, especially since Solomon was young.

6.10.2.en: 2- To alert him that keeping the commandment is more important than building the house, so he and his people should hold fast to the commandments of God during the building of the house and afterward.

6.11.0.en: I will perform my word: I will carry out what I have pledged.

6.11.1.en: The Lord assured him that if he and the people remained faithful in their conduct, keeping the worship of God and His law, and observed all His commandments to do them, then on His part He would fulfill for them all that He had promised David his father, and would dwell among them and not forsake them.

6.11.2.en: God wants to dwell among us because He loves us and wants to satisfy us with His love and shepherd us. Do we make room for Him in our hearts and give up everything that keeps us from Him .. He wants us to be holy temples for Him in which prayers rise like the fragrance of incense, so that He blesses us with every spiritual blessing we need.

6.12.s.en: (3) The Holy Place and the Holy of Holies

6.12.0.en: Thus Solomon built the Temple of the Lord and finished building it, that is, its outer walls and its roofs of stones and timber, and then it will mention after this the covering of the house on the inside with timber and gold and then adorning them.

6.13.1.en: After the stone walls were built, Solomon wanted to cover them with timber on the inside, so he set up ribs, that is, wooden uprights from the floor to the roof, and then fastened wooden boards to these uprights, which covered the whole wall, and no one could see the stone inside the Temple any longer. The timber lining the walls was of precious cedar wood, which does not spoil or wear out easily, while the floor of the Temple he covered with boards of fir wood, which is also among the precious timbers.

6.14.0.en: The sides of the house: that is, the western part of the Temple, which is a cubic part whose length, width, and height are twenty cubits, that is, ten meters.

6.14.1.en: He even built it within for the oracle: he set apart this part, that is, the rear of the house, to be the place for the Holy of Holies, which he called the oracle, for the ark of the covenant to be put in it; the word "oracle" (mihrab) is applied to the inner chambers in temples, and it is a Greek word meaning the place that one is permitted to enter. Solomon set apart ten meters of the rear of the house for the Holy of Holies and covered its walls entirely from the floor to the roof with boards of cedar wood, and set up a wooden wall from the floor to the roof to separate the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies, and made a door in it, as appears from (v. 31).

6.15.0.en: The rest of the Temple extended in front of the Holy of Holies for a length of 20 meters, and it is the part called the Holy Place, in which are the lampstand, the altar of incense, and the table of the showbread, and only the priests enter it, and it lies on the eastern side of the Holy of Holies.

6.16.1.en: All the walls of the house on the inside were covered with timber, and on them were carved, for adornment, shapes of flowers and gourds, because God rejoices in the spiritual fruits of His children who worship Him, which are symbolized by the flowers and gourds.

6.17.1.en: He prepared an oracle in the midst of the Temple within, in which to put the ark of the covenant of the Lord, since the entrance of the oracle was through the Holy Place, and the oracle was surrounded by the chambers on its three sides, north, west, and south, while the east side was the Holy Place. So the oracle is in the middle because it is surrounded by chambers on three sides, and the fourth side is the Holy Place.

6.17.2.en: The scholar Origen says: "The soul must have an altar in the midst of the heart on which we offer the sacrifices of prayer and the giving of mercy, and on which we slay every evil thought and kill all pride and anger." Let your heart be a sacrifice of the love of God, from which prayers and praises rise every day, and let it be moved with love and kindness toward everyone in need.

6.18.0.en: The length, width, and height of the oracle were ten meters. He covered it with plates of pure gold and beat the gold onto the carved, engraved wood, so that the whole wall appeared as gold engraved with the decorative shapes that were carved on the wood beneath it, and the gold plates were fastened to the wood with gold nails, and therefore nothing was seen inside the oracle but gold, to declare the greatness of the presence of God. Gold also symbolizes heavenly life, so it declares that God's dwelling is in heaven and that in His humility He dwelt among His people, to lift them up and raise them above all earthly desires.

6.18.1.en: The altar of incense, made of stone, which was in the Holy Place, Solomon overlaid with cedar wood and then overlaid the wood with gold. This is the golden altar, that is, the altar of incense on which incense is offered every day inside the Holy Place before the oracle, that is, the Holy of Holies. It is noticed that this altar in the tabernacle of meeting was made of acacia wood and overlaid with gold because it was carried with the equipment of the tabernacle, while here, for the permanence of the Temple, it was made of stone (Ex 30:1-8).

6.19.0.en: In this way Solomon covered the whole Temple on the inside with pure gold, that is, the stone walls covered with timber and likewise the wooden wall separating the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies, the wooden one made in it. So nothing was seen inside the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies but gold. He drew chains of gold before the door, which are lifted only once a year, so that the priests might enter through this main door on the great Day of Atonement (Lev 16). From the above appears the tight closing of the Holy of Holies to show the glory of God, which no one can behold. Only the high priest is permitted once a year, as a type of Christ our High Priest, who ascended into heaven once after His Resurrection to prepare a place for us and take us to Himself, which is the Kingdom of Heaven. The way into the holiest in the Old Testament was closed because of our sins, and Christ the Redeemer opened it in the New Testament to bring us with Him into heaven. It is noticed that the oracle, which is the Holy of Holies, has no windows, because it is a type of heaven, which has no need of the sun or the moon for their rays to enter through the windows, because Christ is the light of heaven. The only light in the Holy of Holies was a divine light called the light of the Shekinah, which the high priest sees between the two cherubim that are on the ark.

6.20.0.en: The altar that was by the oracle: the altar of incense, which is in the Holy Place, which is called the house and is in front of the Holy of Holies, which is called the oracle, and incense is raised upon it before the oracle; therefore it was called the altar of the oracle.

6.20.1.en: The whole Temple was overlaid on the inside with pure gold, including the altar of the oracle, and this required large quantities of gold. David had left Solomon a great amount of gold (1 Chr 22:14), in addition to Solomon's income of gold, which was 666 talents in one year (ch. 10:14). Gold was used only rarely for minting gold coins. So Solomon had large quantities of gold available to build the house of the Lord.

6.20.3.en: 1- Solomon's care that the Temple of God be furnished with the finest materials, which was gold, at that time, out of his feeling that it was the greatest place in the world.

6.20.4.en: 2- To help the priests during their service to feel reverence before God and a sense of His presence.

6.20.5.en: 3- Gold symbolizes heavenly life, so it gives the priests a sense of longing for heaven, where the throne of God is.

6.20.6.en: The overlaying of the Temple with gold shows the extent of Solomon's love and care for the house of the Lord, and it gladdens God's heart that you offer Him the dearest thing you have, and if you have only little, God rejoices in your gifts however small they are, like the gift of the widow with the two mites. What matters is that you show your love for God by giving as much as you can.

6.21.0.en: Two cherubim: the dual of cherub, an angel of the rank of the cherubim or sharubim who are full of eyes, and who represents divine justice.

6.21.1.en: Solomon made two cherubim, the height of each ten cubits, and their wings spread on their two sides, and from the tip of the wing of the cherub to the other tip ten cubits. He set up the two cherubim next to each other, so that the tip of the wing of one cherub touched the tip of the wing of the other cherub. The two cherubim stood on the floor of the Holy of Holies, and the tip of the wing of each cherub reached the wall, that is, the cherubim reach between the north and south walls and stand beside the ark and look toward the Holy Place, which is called the house; they represent divine justice. When the high priest sprinkles the blood on the ark on the great Day of Atonement every year, the two cherubim, that is, divine justice, see the blood and God pardons His people. The blood of animals, as we know, is a type of the blood of Christ the Savior, by which we obtain forgiveness.

6.21.2.en: The two cherubim were made of olive wood, which is among the finest timbers. From the olive comes the oil, which is a type of the Holy Spirit, and the olive leaf is a type of peace; that is, the two cherubim are a type of the Spirit of God, who by the blood of Christ is pleased with us and forgives our sins and gives us peace. And because the dimensions of the Holy of Holies, which is called the oracle, are twenty cubits in length and twenty cubits in width, the two cherubim fill the whole space from the north wall to the south, while the roof is twenty cubits high and the height of the cherub is ten cubits, so their height is half the height of the oracle.

6.21.3.en: Then he overlaid the two cherubim with gold, because they are angels who symbolize heavenly life, since, as we mentioned, gold symbolizes heaven, so they declare that the oracle is an image of heaven on earth.

6.21.4.en: These two cherubim are different from the two cherubim on the cover of the ark, and they differ from them in the following:

6.21.5.en: 1- These two cherubim stand on the floor, while the other two are on the cover of the ark.

6.21.6.en: 2- The face of these two cherubim is turned toward the Holy Place, while the other two look toward the cover of the ark, where the blood is sprinkled, and divine justice, which is represented by these two cherubim above the cover, is satisfied. But these two cherubim standing on the floor have their faces toward the Holy Place, to declare the justice of God and His awe before those standing in the Holy Place.

6.21.7.en: 3- These two cherubim are made of wood and overlaid with gold, while the other two are made of gold and are one piece with the cover.

6.21.8.en: 4- The wings of these two cherubim standing on the floor extend from wall to wall, and the wing of each touches the other, so they are the front that the high priest sees when he enters the Holy of Holies, while the two sculpted cherubim on the cover look down toward the cover and the tips of their wings touch, so their form is arched, while the two on the floor are flat in form.

6.21.9.en: The Church is the image of heaven on earth; in it we receive the Body and Blood of the Lord to be united with us, so that He lifts our eyes to heaven that we may live for God and not for the world. So enter the Church with submission, knowing that you stand before God, and bow down before His sanctuary and thank Him for His grace that He has brought you into His house.

6.22.s.en: (4) The adornment of the Temple and the time of its building

6.22.0.en: The house: what is meant by it here is the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies.

6.22.1.en: On all the walls of the Temple he carved drawings of cherubim, palm trees, buds, and flowers, on the inside of the Temple, that is, in the house and the oracle, which are the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies, and also on the outside, that is, on the walls of the outer porch in front of the house (v. 3). The cherubim, as we mentioned, their presence symbolizes the angels and heavenly life within the house of the Lord. Palm trees in the wilderness protect dwellings and tents, so they symbolize protection, security, and peace.

6.22.2.en: The buds and flowers symbolize the spiritual fruits that the Holy Spirit gives to His children who worship Him. When the priests and the people see these drawings, they are encouraged in spiritual striving to adorn themselves with virtues.

6.22.3.en: The carving of the cherubim, palm trees, buds, and flowers was engraved in the wood and then covered with gold, so they became golden carvings that everyone who enters the Holy Place sees.

6.23.0.en: He overlaid the floor of the Temple, made of fir wood, with gold, both inside, that is, in the Holy of Holies, and outside, that is, in the Holy Place, to declare the heavenly glory of God, and everyone who enters the house of the Lord feels submission before Him and awe of Him.

6.24.1.en: Lintel: the upper post of the door.

6.24.2.en: The side posts: the two side posts in which the door is fixed.

6.24.3.en: A fifth part: equal to a fifth of the width of the wall.

6.24.4.en: There was a wooden wall separating the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies (v. 21), in which Solomon made a door of two leaves whose width was a fifth of the width of the wall, that is, its width was four cubits; that is, each leaf with its side post fastened to it was two cubits wide.

6.25.0.en: He made the two leaves of the door of olive wood and carved on them drawings of cherubim, palm trees, and buds of flowers, then covered the two leaves of the door with gold, so that the carved shapes in the door and the projecting parts appeared in it, and their form was very beautiful, that is, inlaid with gold.

6.26.0.en: The door of the temple: that is, the outer entrance of the Holy Place, which is on the east side.

6.26.1.en: Squared: that is, the width of the door was a quarter of the width of the wall; the wall was twenty cubits wide, so the width of the door with its posts was five cubits.

6.26.2.en: Two folding leaves: the door leaf consisted of two leaves joined by hinges, one folding upon the other.

6.26.3.en: The entrance of the Temple, that is, the house or the Holy Place, consisted of a wooden wall in which a door was made five cubits wide, and the door had two leaves, each leaf made up of two sections folding one upon the other, so that the door opened fully. The door of the Holy Place was wider than the door of the Holy of Holies, because the priests enter the Holy Place every day, so its width was five cubits, while the Holy of Holies was four cubits wide, since only the high priest enters it, once a year. It is noticed that all the timber of the door was of the precious kind, which is olive wood or fir.

6.27.1.en: He carved on the two leaves the carving of cherubim, palm trees, buds, and flowers and overlaid them with beaten gold, so the shapes of the cherubim and the rest of the carvings appeared as though sculpted and made of gold, and they were very beautiful. It is understood from this that the gold was thin sheets that could be beaten to take the shape of the carvings engraved in the wood, so the shapes appear as though made of gold.

6.28.0.en: In front of the Holy Place there was the inner court, also called the court of the priests, a courtyard in which were the bronze altar and the lavers, and it had two walls on its sides. Each wall was made of three rows of stones laid one above another with a row of cedar wood on top of them to fasten and adorn them. This court is distinct from another court after it called the court of the people, or the outer court, or the great court. And let us not forget that in the tabernacle of meeting there was only one outer courtyard in front of the Holy Place. The court of the priests is called the upper court (Jer 36:10), because it was on a higher level than the court of the people, so that the people could watch the priests as they performed the various rites of worship (2 Chr 4:9).

6.29.0.en: The month Zif: corresponds to the months of April and May, that is, it takes a part of both months.

6.29.1.en: The month Bul: corresponds to the months of October and November.

6.29.2.en: The building of the Temple began in the fourth year of Solomon's reign in the month of Zif and continued until the eleventh year of his reign in the month of Bul, that is, it took seven and a half years, because it began in the month of Zif, which is the second month of the fourth year, and continued to the month of Bul, which is the eighth month of the eleventh year, so the period is seven years and six months, apart from the period of preparing the timber and materials with which the house was built. We see that Solomon made everything inside the Holy Place, or outside it, new, with measurements different from those in the tabernacle of meeting, but the only thing he did not change from the tabernacle of meeting was the ark of the covenant of God, which he took as it was and placed in the oracle, which is the Holy of Holies, for it represents the presence of God, and with God there is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.

6.29.3.en: It is noticed that the work on the Temple had a spirit distinct from the other works, the most important points of which are:

6.29.4.en: 1- Care and enthusiasm, for they worked energetically because it was the house of God, that is, more important than any other house in the world.

6.29.5.en: 2- The work was done with precision according to the specifications God declared and not according to the ideas of men, however artistic they were.

6.29.6.en: 3- Quietly, for the timber and stones were not cut at the building place and the sound of a chisel was not heard, so the work was done quietly, and this suits the works of God, since they must be far from noise.

6.29.7.en: 4- The work was done with joy because it is a great blessing for everyone who works in the house of the Lord.

6.29.8.en: The tabernacle of meeting declares the presence of God among His people, and its extension is Solomon's Temple; it is a type of the Church in the New Testament, and all of it is a type of the heavenly Jerusalem, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven, for all of it declares the presence of God among His people. The difference between the Church and Solomon's Temple is that it was not permitted for anyone but the priests to enter the Holy Place, and as for the Holy of Holies, the high priest alone enters it once a year, while in the Church all the people enter it, and even partake of the Body and Blood of the Lord and are united with Him, and the Church receives all believers whether of Jewish or Gentile origin.

6.29.9.en: Solomon's Temple has hidden parts that no one sees but the high priest, namely the Holy of Holies or oracle, while in the Church of the New Testament everything is open to the believers on earth, and the only hidden part is the triumphant Church in heaven, and even this appears to some believers in the appearances of the saints. And as the shapes of the cherubim were drawn on the walls of the Temple and its doors, so the angels fill the Church and surround the believers.

6.29.10.en: God's love has made you a temple of the Holy Spirit, so that God may dwell in you always by His Holy Spirit and give you His Body and Blood to be united with Him. You are prepared for God's dwelling, and to dwell in heaven; so remember this always, so that you keep away from every sin and draw near to God and enjoy fellowship with Him.

6.29.11.en: Solomon builds his palace and prepares the components of the Temple. Note: see the drawings and pictures at the end of the book.
